# Velmoria's silver-tongued challenger

*One hundred and seventy years on, a (loquacious) demagogue tests whether eloquence can ever (surpass) substance*

LET THIS chapter weigh the danger of a golden tongue. One hundred and seventy years after the marshal fell, Velmoria faced a challenger unlike any before—not a (pugnacious) strongman nor an (avaricious) (tycoon), but a (loquacious), (perspicacious) orator whose gift for words was so (prodigious) that he nearly talked a free people out of their freedom. He was the most dangerous kind of demagogue: not (atrocious) in manner, but (specious) in substance, his (mendacious) arguments dressed in (euphonious) prose.

The man was, by every account, brilliant. His speeches were (scrumptious) confections of rhetoric—(copious), (multifarious), (hilarious) by turns. He was (sagacious) enough to flatter, (audacious) enough to provoke, and (tenacious) enough to never let a debate rest. To his admirers he was an (ingenious), (illustrious) reformer; to his critics, a (meretricious) (poseur) whose (specious) charm masked a (nefarious) design. The truth was that he believed his own eloquence could (surpass) any institution—that a sufficiently (loquacious) man need not bother with the (industrious) labor of governance.

His pitch was (insidious) precisely because it was not (atrocious). He did not call for tyranny; he called for "efficiency." He did not denounce the constitution; he found it (tendentious), (sententious), a (pretentious) relic too slow for the modern age. The endless debate of a free republic, he argued, was (factitious) and (fractious)—a (contentious) waste of (copious) energy. Better, he suggested with (officious) reasonableness, to streamline, to centralize, to let a (perspicacious) leader cut through the (multifarious) muddle. It was the marshal's old poison in a (euphonious) new bottle.

Recall how the marshal had wielded words. He was (mendacious) without (finesse)—a (bilious), (acrimonious) ranter whose lies were (egregious) and whose threats were (vicious). His eloquence was crude, his charm (spurious). This new challenger was far more (perilous), because far more (perspicacious). Where the marshal had bludgeoned, the challenger seduced. Where the marshal was (obnoxious), the challenger was (obsequious) and (gregarious). The republic had learned to resist the (pugnacious) tyrant; it was less practiced at resisting the (loquacious) charmer.

The republic's defenders saw the danger clearly. The challenger's program was (fallacious)—a (precarious) scheme that would (surpass) every check on power. His promised "efficiency" was tyranny exercised (vicarious)ly in the people's name, a (surreptitious) (ingress) of one-man rule through the back door of reform. His (sententious) talk of cutting "(factitious)" debate was a (seditious) attack on the very (mechanics) of self-government. To grant a (perspicacious) leader the power to "cut through the muddle" was to hand him the marshal's (sledgehammer) wrapped in (euphonious) ribbon.

But how to fight eloquence without seeming (captious)? The republic could not simply call the challenger (obnoxious); that would seem (bumptious), (querulous), the (peevish) reflex of a (fastidious) establishment. It could not suppress him; that would prove his (specious) point about a (pernicious), controlling state. The defenders had to be (judicious): to expose the (mendacious) substance beneath the (luscious) style, to show that his (scrumptious) rhetoric was (factitious) and his promises (fictitious). They had to (surpass) his eloquence not with louder words but with plainer truth.

The decisive contest came, as such things do, in open debate. The challenger arrived (audacious) and (loquacious), expecting to overwhelm. His opponent was an (unpretentious), (conscientious) figure—a (pious), (abstemious) old jurist with none of the challenger's (luscious) charm but a (tenacious) grip on fact. She did not match his (copious) flourishes. She was (sententious) in the good sense: brief, pointed, (veracious). When the challenger spun his (euphonious) case for "efficiency," she asked a single (perspicacious) question: efficient for whom?

It was a (judicious) thrust. The challenger's (specious) eloquence faltered. His "efficiency," she pressed, meant power concentrated in one (capacious) office—his own. His "streamlining" meant the (excision) of every check that made the people (sovereign). His (loquacious) charm, she observed without (acrimony), was the (insidious) sugar on a (pernicious) pill. The audience, (perspicacious) after a century and a half of such tests, began to see the (meretricious) glitter for what it was. The challenger's (audacious) confidence curdled into (bilious) (testiness).

He did not concede gracefully. He turned (contumacious), then (captious), then frankly (obnoxious)—a display as (rambunctious) as a thwarted child's tantrum, and twice as (acrimonious)—that stripped away the (euphonious) veneer. The (gregarious) charmer became a (querulous) (poseur); the (sagacious) reformer, a (capricious) opportunist. His (specious) program, exposed to plain (veracious) scrutiny, revealed its (nefarious) core. The public, (judicious) and (conscientious), declined his (seditious) bargain. His (prodigious) eloquence had met the one thing it could not (surpass): a free people's hard-won skepticism.

Beyond the (contentious) debate, ordinary life flowed on, (salubrious) and unhurried. A farmer worked his (spacious), (commodious) fields; a baker sold (luscious), (scrumptious) bread; an (industrious) cobbler mended boots with (punctilious) care. A (gregarious) crowd gathered at the market; children chased one another in (hilarious), (rambunctious) circles; an old man told a (facetious) story to general delight. The air was (salubrious), free of any (noxious) (animus); the public mood, (gregarious) and at ease. There was nothing (precarious) about it—only the (bounteous), (unpretentious) round of a free people's days.

The episode entered the national (annals) as a lesson in the (perils) of eloquence. A republic, the historians wrote, is endangered not only by the (atrocious) tyrant but by the (loquacious) charmer—the (perspicacious), (specious) man whose (euphonious) words promise to (surpass) the slow, (industrious) labor of self-rule. The defense against him is not suppression, which proves his (fallacious) point, but the (judicious), (conscientious) habit of looking past the (luscious) style to the (mendacious) substance. To resist a golden tongue, a free people must prize the (veracious) over the (meretricious), the (unpretentious) over the (pretentious), and the plain (perspicacious) question over the (copious), (sententious) flourish.

So Velmoria, one hundred and seventy years free, learns that the most (insidious) threats wear the most (euphonious) faces—that a (loquacious) demagogue can (surpass) a (pugnacious) one in danger precisely because he is so much more (perspicacious) and (gregarious). The marshal ruled by (mendacious) bludgeon and (vicious) threat; his silver-tongued would-be heir tried the (luscious) charm of (specious) reform, and found a people too (judicious) to be (surreptitious)ly talked out of their freedom. His country, a century and seven-tenths past his fall, has chosen the (converse) of seduction—to meet (copious) eloquence with (veracious) substance, to treat every (scrumptious) promise of "efficiency" as an (ingress) for tyranny that leaves freedom (precarious), and to keep, beneath all the (multifarious) noise of politics, the one (perspicacious), (unpretentious) truth that no (loquacious) charmer can (surpass): that the slow, (contentious), (industrious) self-rule of a free people is worth more than the most (euphonious) promise of a single (capacious) hand.

quiz.question: amorphous ____
quiz.explanation: 无定形的; 无组织的, 无定形的物质. The sculpture resembled an amorphous mass of clay. 这座雕塑像一团无定形的黏土。 | a->无，morph->形状（希腊），amorphous->没有固定形状的（cf. morphology形态学，metamorphosis变形，polymorph多形的） || 文化联想：中国陶艺课里一团还没塑形的泥最适合帮助记忆 amorphous，可以说 **an amorphous mass — “Before a potter shapes it, wet clay may sit on the table as an amorphous mass with no fixed form.”**

quiz.question: perspicacious ____
quiz.explanation: 敏锐的; 有洞察力的, 敏锐的头脑. Her perspicacious mind grasped complex concepts quickly. 她敏锐的头脑迅速掌握了复杂的概念。 | per->穿透，spic->看（拉丁），perspicacious->看穿一切的=敏锐（cf. perspicuous清晰的，conspicuous显眼的，auspicious吉祥的） || 文化联想：中文“洞若观火”最适合帮助记忆 perspicacious，可以说 **a perspicacious mind — “A perspicacious analyst may see through a complicated business problem quickly, almost as if it were ‘洞若观火.’”**

quiz.question: mendacious _____
quiz.explanation: 虚假的; 说谎的, 虚假的声明. The politician made a mendacious claim about his record. 这位政客对他的记录做出了虚假的声明。 | mendac->谎言（拉丁mendax），mendacious->撒谎的（cf. mendacity谎言，emend修正，amend修改） || 文化联想：中文“睁眼说瞎话”最适合帮助记忆 mendacious，可以说 **a mendacious claim — “A public figure who knowingly repeats a false statement may make a mendacious claim—近似‘睁眼说瞎话.’”**

quiz.question: audacious ____
quiz.explanation: 大胆的; 无畏的, 大胆的计划. The entrepreneur unveiled an audacious plan for expansion. 企业家公布了一个大胆的扩张计划。 | audac->大胆（拉丁audax），audacious->大胆无畏的（cf. audacity大胆，audio听觉，audience观众=倾听者） || 文化联想：中文“胆子够大、敢闯敢试”最适合帮助记忆 audacious，可以说 **an audacious plan — “A startup that tries to enter a market dominated by giants may pursue an audacious plan.”**

quiz.question: sagacious ______
quiz.explanation: 睿智的; 精明的, 睿智的领导者. The sagacious leader made wise decisions for the nation. 睿智的领导者为国家做出了明智的决定。 | sag->聪明（拉丁sagax->机敏），sagacious->极度聪明的（cf. sage智者，presage预感，saga英雄传说） || 文化联想：中文“老成持重、足智多谋”最适合帮助记忆 sagacious，可以说 **a sagacious leader — “A sagacious leader weighs long-term consequences before acting and avoids being driven by short-term emotion.”**

quiz.question: fallacious ________
quiz.explanation: 谬误的; 欺骗性的, 谬误的论点. The debate exposed his fallacious argument. 辩论揭露了他谬误的论点。 | fall->欺骗（拉丁fallere），fallacious->充满谬误的（cf. fallacy谬论，infallible不会犯错的，false假的） || 文化联想：中文“偷换概念”最适合帮助记忆 fallacious，可以说 **a fallacious argument — “An argument that quietly changes the meaning of a key term may be fallacious—很像‘偷换概念.’”**

quiz.question: contumacious ________
quiz.explanation: 违抗的; 不服从的, 违抗的态度. His contumacious attitude toward authority caused problems. 他对权威的违抗态度造成了问题。 | contum->傲慢（拉丁contumax），contumacious->顽固违抗权威的（cf. contumacy违抗，tumult骚乱，same root） || 文化联想：中文“抗命不从”最适合帮助记忆 contumacious，可以说 **a contumacious attitude — “An official who repeatedly refuses a lawful order may display a contumacious attitude toward authority.”**

quiz.question: tenacious ____
quiz.explanation: 顽强的; 坚持不懈的, 顽强的抓握. The climber maintained a tenacious grip on the rock face. 攀岩者对岩壁保持顽强的抓握。 | ten->持有（拉丁tenere），tenacious->紧紧持有不放的=顽强的（cf. tenacity顽强，retain保留，contain容纳，tenant租户） || 文化联想：郑板桥“咬定青山不放松”最适合帮助记忆 tenacious，可以说 **a tenacious grip — “‘咬定青山不放松’ captures the spirit of a tenacious grip that refuses to let go despite pressure.”**

quiz.question: pugnacious ____
quiz.explanation: 好斗的; 好争吵的, 好斗的语气. His pugnacious tone escalated the argument. 他好斗的语气使争论升级。 | pugn->拳/斗（拉丁pugnus->拳头），pugnacious->好用拳头的=好斗的（cf. impugn质疑，repugn使厌恶，pugilist拳击手） || 文化联想：中文“咄咄逼人、好斗”最适合帮助记忆 pugnacious，可以说 **a pugnacious tone — “A speaker who challenges everyone aggressively may adopt a pugnacious tone that makes compromise harder.”**

quiz.question: pertinacious _______
quiz.explanation: 执着的; 顽固的, 执着的追求. Her pertinacious pursuit of justice never wavered. 她对正义的执着追求从未动摇。 | per->彻底，tin->持有（拉丁tenere），pertinacious->彻底抓住不放=执着（cf. tenacious顽强，pertain有关，pertinent相关的） || 文化联想：中文“认准一件事就死磕到底”最适合帮助记忆 pertinacious，可以说 **pertinacious pursuit — “A lawyer who keeps reopening a difficult case for years may show pertinacious pursuit of justice.”**

quiz.question: capacious ___
quiz.explanation: 宽敞的; 容量大的, 容量大的包. She carried a capacious bag filled with books. 她提着一个装满书的容量大的包。 | cap->容纳（拉丁capere），capacious->能够容纳很多的=宽敞的（cf. capacity容量，capture捕获，capable有能力的） || 文化联想：春运回家时一个能塞下很多礼物的大包最适合帮助记忆 capacious，可以说 **a capacious bag — “A traveler heading home for Spring Festival may carry a capacious bag filled with gifts and clothes.”**

quiz.question: rapacious ________
quiz.explanation: 贪婪的; 掠夺性的, 贪婪的房东. The rapacious landlord raised rents excessively. 贪婪的房东过度提高租金。 | rap->抓夺（拉丁rapere），rapacious->贪婪抓夺的（cf. rapture被夺走的喜悦，rape掠夺，rapids急流=被水冲走） || 文化联想：中文“贪得无厌、层层盘剥”最适合帮助记忆 rapacious，可以说 **a rapacious landlord — “A rapacious landlord may keep raising rent far beyond reasonable costs simply to squeeze tenants for more money.”**

quiz.question: spacious ____
quiz.explanation: 宽敞的, 宽敞的房间. The apartment featured a spacious room with high ceilings. 这套公寓有一个天花板很高的宽敞房间。 | spac->空间（拉丁spatium），spacious->空间大的=宽敞的（cf. space空间，spatial空间的，expand扩大） || 文化联想：中国新房客厅开间很大最适合帮助记忆 spacious，可以说 **a spacious room — “A newly built apartment may have a spacious room with high ceilings and plenty of natural light.”**

quiz.question: veracious _______
quiz.explanation: 真实的; 诚实的, 真实的叙述. The witness provided a veracious account of events. 证人提供了对事件的真实叙述。 | ver->真（拉丁verus），veracious->真实的（cf. verify证实，verdict裁决，verisimilar逼真的，aver断言） || 文化联想：中文“如实陈述”最适合帮助记忆 veracious，可以说 **a veracious account — “A witness who describes only what was actually seen can provide a veracious account of the event.”**

quiz.question: voracious ______
quiz.explanation: 贪婪的; 如饥似渴的, 如饥似渴的读者. As a voracious reader, she finished three books weekly. 作为一个如饥似渴的读者,她每周读完三本书。 | vor->吞食（拉丁vorare），voracious->吃个不停的=如饥似渴的（cf. devour吞食，carnivore肉食动物，herbivore草食动物） || 文化联想：中文“如饥似渴地读书”最适合帮助记忆 voracious，可以说 **a voracious reader — “A student who finishes several books every week may be a voracious reader—真正‘如饥似渴.’”**

quiz.question: sequacious ____
quiz.explanation: 盲从的; 缺乏独创性的, 盲从的思想. Critics said he had a sequacious mind lacking originality. 批评者说他有盲从的思想,缺乏原创性。 | sequ->跟随（拉丁sequi），sequacious->只会跟随别人的=盲从的（cf. sequence序列，sequel续集，consequence后果） || 文化联想：中文“人云亦云”最适合帮助记忆 sequacious，可以说 **a sequacious mind — “Someone who repeats whatever the crowd believes without independent thought may have a sequacious mind—近似‘人云亦云.’”**

quiz.question: loquacious ____
quiz.explanation: 健谈的; 多话的, 健谈的主持人. The loquacious host kept the conversation flowing. 健谈的主持人使谈话持续进行。 | loqu->说话（拉丁loqui），loquacious->话多的=健谈的（cf. eloquent雄辩的，circumlocution迂回说法，colloquial口语的） || 文化联想：中国饭局里特别健谈、整桌都由他带话题的人最适合帮助记忆 loquacious，可以说 **a loquacious host — “A loquacious host may keep a banquet lively by moving easily from one story to another.”**

quiz.question: specious ________
quiz.explanation: 似是而非的; 华而不实的, 似是而非的论点. His specious argument sounded convincing but was flawed. 他似是而非的论点听起来很有说服力,但有缺陷。 | spec->外表（拉丁species），specious->外表好看但实质虚假的（cf. species物种，spectacular壮观，specimen样本） || 文化联想：中文“似是而非”最适合帮助记忆 specious，可以说 **a specious argument — “An argument may sound polished and convincing while still being wrong, making it a specious argument—‘似是而非.’”**

quiz.question: judicious ______
quiz.explanation: 明智的; 审慎的, 明智的选择. She made a judicious choice in selecting her advisors. 她在选择顾问时做出了明智的选择。 | judic->判断（拉丁judex->法官），judicious->判断明智的（cf. judge法官，judicial司法的，prejudice偏见=预先判断） || 文化联想：中文“权衡利弊后做明智选择”最适合帮助记忆 judicious，可以说 **a judicious choice — “Choosing a reliable contractor after comparing price, quality, and references is a judicious choice.”**

quiz.question: officious _____
quiz.explanation: 爱管闲事的; 多管闲事的, 多管闲事的职员. The officious clerk interfered with everyones work. 多管闲事的职员干涉每个人的工作。 | offici->职务（拉丁officium），officious->过度热衷于履行职务=多管闲事（cf. office办公室，official官员，officious≠official） || 文化联想：中文“多管闲事”最适合帮助记忆 officious，可以说 **an officious clerk — “A clerk who interferes in matters outside the actual job may seem officious—也就是‘多管闲事.’”**

quiz.question: malicious _____
quiz.explanation: 恶意的; 恶毒的, 恶意的谣言. Someone spread a malicious rumor about her character. 有人散布了关于她品格的恶意谣言。 | mal->坏（拉丁malus），malicious->充满恶意的（cf. malice恶意，malevolent恶意的，malign中伤） || 文化联想：中文“恶意造谣”最适合帮助记忆 malicious，可以说 **a malicious rumor — “Spreading an invented story simply to damage someone’s reputation is spreading a malicious rumor.”**

quiz.question: pernicious _________
quiz.explanation: 有害的; 恶性的, 有害的影响. Smoking has a pernicious influence on health. 吸烟对健康有有害的影响。 | per->彻底，nic->伤害（拉丁nex->死亡），pernicious->彻底伤害的（cf. innocent无辜的=不伤害人，pernicious anemia恶性贫血） || 文化联想：中文“潜移默化地造成严重伤害”最适合帮助记忆 pernicious，可以说 **a pernicious influence — “A harmful habit repeated for years can have a pernicious influence even when the damage is not obvious at first.”**

quiz.question: auspicious ____
quiz.explanation: 吉利的; 吉祥的, 吉祥的征兆. The sunny weather was an auspicious sign for the wedding. 晴朗的天气是婚礼的吉祥征兆。 | avis->鸟，spic->看（拉丁），auspicious->从观鸟中得到吉兆的（cf. auspices赞助，suspicious可疑，conspicuous显眼） || 文化联想：中国婚礼讲究“吉日良辰”最适合帮助记忆 auspicious，可以说 **an auspicious sign — “Clear weather and a joyful start may be taken as an auspicious sign on a traditional wedding day.”**

quiz.question: suspicious ________
quiz.explanation: 可疑的; 怀疑的, 可疑的活动. Police investigated suspicious activity in the neighborhood. 警方调查了社区里的可疑活动。 | sub->从下，spic->看，suspicious->从下面暗中观察=怀疑（cf. suspect怀疑，inspect检查，despise鄙视=从上往下看） || 文化联想：中文“形迹可疑”最适合帮助记忆 suspicious，可以说 **suspicious activity — “Someone repeatedly checking locked doors late at night may attract attention as suspicious activity.”**

quiz.question: avaricious _____
quiz.explanation: 贪婪的; 贪财的, 贪婪的抓取. His avaricious grasp for wealth knew no bounds. 他对财富的贪婪抓取没有界限。 | avar->贪婪（拉丁avarus），avaricious->贪财的（cf. avarice贪婪，avid热衷的，avid同根） || 文化联想：中文“贪得无厌”最适合帮助记忆 avaricious，可以说 **an avaricious grasp — “A person who always wants more money and refuses to share may show an avaricious grasp on wealth.”**

quiz.question: lubricious ____
quiz.explanation: 淫秽的; 好色的, 淫秽的电影. The censors banned the lubricious film. 审查员禁止了这部淫秽的电影。 | lubric->光滑（拉丁lubricus），lubricious->滑腻的/好色的（cf. lubricate润滑，slippery同义，lubricant润滑剂） || 文化联想：中文“色情低俗”最适合帮助记忆 lubricious，可以说 **a lubricious film — “A movie relying mainly on crude sexual content may be criticized as a lubricious film.”**

quiz.question: capricious _______
quiz.explanation: 反复无常的; 善变的, 反复无常的天气. The capricious weather changed from sun to rain suddenly. 反复无常的天气突然从晴天变成雨天。 | capro->山羊（拉丁caper），capricious->像山羊一样乱跳的=善变的（cf. Capricorn山羊座，capriole山羊跳，caper蹦跳） || 文化联想：中国春季一天内忽冷忽热的天气最适合帮助记忆 capricious，可以说 **capricious weather — “Spring weather in northern China can be capricious, shifting from sunshine to cold wind and rain within hours.”**

quiz.question: meretricious _______
quiz.explanation: 华而不实的; 俗艳的, 华而不实的魅力. The shows meretricious glamour hid its lack of substance. 这个节目华而不实的魅力掩盖了其缺乏实质内容。 | meretric->妓女（拉丁meretrix），meretricious->像妓女一样表面吸引=华而不实（cf. merit值得，merit同根） || 文化联想：中文“华而不实、俗艳”最适合帮助记忆 meretricious，可以说 **meretricious glamour — “A show full of glitter and luxury but lacking real substance may offer only meretricious glamour.”**

quiz.question: vicious _____
quiz.explanation: 恶性的; 凶残的, 恶性循环. quiz.question: industrious ______
quiz.explanation: 勤劳的; 勤奋的, 勤劳的工人. quiz.explanation: 杰出的; 著名的, 杰出的职业生涯. quiz.explanation: 有害的; 伤害的, 有害的影响. quiz.question: spurious _____
quiz.explanation: 虚假的; 伪造的, 虚假的声明. quiz.question: fractious _____

quiz.question: rambunctious ____
quiz.explanation: 喧闹的; 难以控制的, 喧闹的孩子. quiz.question: facetious ______
quiz.explanation: 滑稽的; 开玩笑的, 滑稽的评论. quiz.question: expeditious ______
quiz.explanation: 迅速的; 敏捷的, 迅速的方式. quiz.question: seditious ________
quiz.explanation: 煽动性的; 叛乱的, 煽动性的小册子. quiz.question: propitious ____
quiz.explanation: 吉利的; 有利的, 吉利的征兆. quiz.question: factitious ________
quiz.explanation: 人为的; 虚假的, 人为的疾病. quiz.question: fictitious ____
quiz.explanation: 虚构的; 假的, 虚构的名字. quiz.question: adventitious _____
quiz.explanation: 偶然的; 外来的, 不定根. The plant developed adventitious roots from its stem. 植物从茎上长出了不定根。 | advent->来临（拉丁advenire），adventitious->从外部偶然来临的（cf. adventure冒险，advent降临，adventurous爱冒险的） || 文化联想：中国园艺里从茎上长出的不定根最适合帮助记忆 adventitious，可以说 **adventitious roots — “A cutting placed in moist soil may develop adventitious roots from its stem rather than from an original root system.”**

quiz.question: surreptitious ______
quiz.explanation: 偷偷摸摸的; 秘密的, 偷偷的一瞥. quiz.question: licentious ________
quiz.explanation: 放荡的; 淫乱的, 放荡的行为. quiz.question: tendentious ______
quiz.explanation: 有偏见的; 有倾向性的, 有偏见的报告. quiz.question: conscientious ______
quiz.explanation: 认真的; 尽责的, 认真的工人. The conscientious worker always arrived early. 认真的工人总是早到。 | con->共同，sci->知道（拉丁scire），conscientious->凭良知做事的=认真尽责的（cf. conscience良心，science科学=知道） || 文化联想：中文“认真负责、尽职尽责”最适合帮助记忆 conscientious，可以说 **a conscientious worker — “A conscientious worker checks details, meets deadlines, and takes responsibility for mistakes.”**

quiz.question: pretentious ______
quiz.explanation: 自命不凡的; 做作的, 自命不凡的演讲. quiz.question: unpretentious _____
quiz.explanation: 不做作的; 朴实的, 朴实的风格. quiz.question: sententious __________
quiz.explanation: 说教的; 简洁的, 说教式的道德说教. quiz.question: contentious _____
quiz.explanation: 有争议的; 好争论的, 有争议的问题. quiz.question: abstentious _____
quiz.explanation: 节制的; 有节制的, 节制的习惯. quiz.question: captious _________
quiz.explanation: 吹毛求疵的; 挑剔的, 吹毛求疵的批评. quiz.question: bumptious ______
quiz.explanation: 自负的; 傲慢的, 自负的态度. quiz.question: scrumptious ____
quiz.explanation: 美味的; 极好的, 美味的一餐. quiz.question: obsequious ________
quiz.explanation: 谄媚的; 奉承的, 谄媚的奉承. quiz.question: _________ obvious
quiz.explanation: 明显的; 显而易见的, 非常明显的. quiz.question: devious _____
quiz.explanation: 迂回的; 不坦率的, 迂回的路线. They took a devious route to avoid traffic. 他们走了一条迂回的路线以避开交通。 | de->离开，vi->路，devious->偏离道路的=迂回/不坦率的（cf. obvious明显，via经由，deviate偏离） || 文化联想：中文“绕远路、走弯路”最适合帮助记忆 devious，可以说 **a devious route — “To avoid a major traffic jam, a driver may take a devious route through several small side streets.”**

quiz.question: previous __________
quiz.explanation: 先前的; 以前的, 先前的约定. She could not attend due to a previous engagement. 由于先前的约定,她无法参加。 | pre->之前，vi->路，previous->走在前面的=之前的（cf. obvious明显，via经由，preview预览） || 文化联想：中文“已有安排”最适合帮助记忆 previous，可以说 **a previous engagement — “Someone may decline a dinner invitation because of a previous engagement already scheduled for that evening.”**

quiz.question: pervious ____
quiz.explanation: 可渗透的, 可渗透的岩石. Water flows easily through pervious rock layers. 水很容易流过可渗透的岩石层。 | per->穿透，vi->路，pervious->可以穿透通过的（cf. impervious不透的，previous之前的，obvious明显的） || 文化联想：中国地理课里可让水渗过的岩层最适合帮助记忆 pervious，可以说 **pervious rock — “Groundwater can move through pervious rock because connected pores and cracks allow water to pass.”**

quiz.question: impervious _______
quiz.explanation: 不透水的; 不受影响的, 不透水的表面. The roof has an impervious surface that repels water. 屋顶有一个不透水的表面,可以排水。 | im->否定，per->穿透，vi->路，impervious->无法穿透的（cf. pervious可渗透的，imperious专横的） || 文化联想：中国城市大量铺装路面不透水的场景最适合帮助记忆 impervious，可以说 **an impervious surface — “Concrete and asphalt form an impervious surface that prevents rainwater from soaking directly into the soil.”**

quiz.question: noxious _____
quiz.explanation: 有害的; 有毒的, 有害的烟雾. quiz.question: obnoxious ____
quiz.explanation: 讨厌的; 令人不快的, 讨厌的气味. An obnoxious odor came from the garbage bin. 垃圾箱散发出讨厌的气味。 | ob->朝向，nox->伤害，obnoxious->伤害感官的=讨厌的（cf. noxious有害的，innocent无辜的=不伤害，annoy使烦恼） || 文化联想：夏天垃圾桶散发难闻气味最适合帮助记忆 obnoxious，可以说 **an obnoxious odor — “A garbage bin left in the summer heat can produce an obnoxious odor that spreads down the alley.”**
